title: Laredo Voters Face Three Races on the December Ballot
excerpt: Laredo voters will decide three races in December: the District 8 special election on Dec. 5, and the mayoral runoff and Laredo College Board Position 9 runoff on Dec. 12, according to KGNS.
content:
Laredo voters have three races to keep track of in December, following the midterm elections, according to KGNS.

The first is the District 8 special election, set for Saturday, Dec. 5. Early voting for that race runs from Nov. 23 through Dec. 1, according to KGNS. The article names no candidates for the District 8 race.

The second is the mayoral runoff, which voters will decide on Saturday, Dec. 12. Council member Alyssa Cigarroa faces Mayor Victor Treviño, according to KGNS.

The third is the Laredo College Board of Trustees Position 9 runoff, also decided on Dec. 12. Incumbent Tita Vela faces Eduardo Lopez, according to KGNS. Early voting for that race runs from Nov. 30 through Dec. 8.

KGNS did not publish early-voting times or polling locations for any of the three races in the article.

Update — November 18, 2026

A debate over polling locations for the District 8 special election ended in a stalemate at City Hall on Monday, Nov. 16, according to KGNS. Councilwoman Alyssa Cigarroa asked the city to add the Marcos Aranda Recreation Center as a polling site, calling the current situation a "failure of management." Councilwoman Melissa Cigarroa also opposed the current polling plan, saying, "To purposefully close down a site in a district where it gets the highest vote totals is fundamentally unfair and undemocratic."

Alyssa Cigarroa said the only other west-side option for voters is the Webb County Elections Office, which she said is frequently blocked by passing trains. City officials said they are unable to make changes to the locations, saying the Secretary of State is blocking modifications because early voting is scheduled to begin Monday, Nov. 23.

The debate ended at 11 p.m., when a state-mandated deadline forced the meeting to adjourn, according to KGNS. Council members were in the process of making a motion to add the recreation center as a site, but the meeting concluded before a vote could be taken.

Source: KGNS, Nov. 16, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 18, 2026.

Update — November 25, 2026

Early voting for the District 8 special election began Monday, Nov. 23, and 257 ballots were cast on the first day, according to election officials cited by Local National. Of those, 185 were cast in person and 72 by mail. The Webb County Elections Office drew the most in-person voters, with 128, followed by Laredo Fire Department No. 1 with 25, Lamar Bruni Vergara Inner City Park with 23, and Gallagher Garden Apartments with nine.

Early voting continues through Tuesday, Dec. 1, at the four sites — the Webb County Elections Office, 720 Convent Ave.; Lamar Bruni Vergara Inner City Park, 202 W. Plum St.; Laredo Fire Department No. 1, 1 Guadalupe St.; and Gallagher Garden Apartments, 5118 Gallagher Ave. — with no voting Thursday, Nov. 26, or Friday, Nov. 27, for Thanksgiving. Election Day is Saturday, Dec. 5.

Update sources: Local National, Nov. 24, 2026; KGNS, Nov. 22, 2026.

Update — November 25, 2026 (evening)

After the second day of early voting, the Webb County Elections Administration reported 435 ballots cast in the District 8 special election, according to KGNS. That includes 354 votes cast in person and 81 mail-in ballots. On Tuesday, Nov. 24, the second day of voting, 178 ballots were cast — 169 in person and nine by mail, according to the county’s early-voting totals.

Early voting continues through Tuesday, Dec. 1, with no voting Thursday, Nov. 26, or Friday, Nov. 27, for Thanksgiving. Election Day is Saturday, Dec. 5.

Update sources: KGNS, Nov. 25, 2026; Webb County Elections Administration early-voting totals, Nov. 25, 2026.
